newsitem.title: JAPAN: Suzuki no comment on Changan B shares.
newsitem.headline: Suzuki no comment on Changan B shares.

text.p: Suzuki Motor Corp on Thursday declined to comment on a media report that it will buy shares of China's Chongqing Changan Automobile Co.
The South China Morning Post reported on Thursday that Suzuki had agreed to buy half of the 250 million B shares issued by the Changan, representing 16.5 percent of the firm.
"We cannot comment on such a report," a Suzuki spokesman said in Tokyo.
Suzuki currently has no stake in the Sichuan province-based Changan, Suzuki's joint-venture partner in Chongqing Suzuki Automobile.
Chongqing Suzuki Automobile, which makes the Alto mini cars, is owned 50 percent by Changan, 35 percent by Suzuki and 15 percent Nissho Iwai Corp.
Industry sources said Suzuki and Changan could not confirm the report because they are waiting for official approval from the central Chinese government.
Chongqing Suzuki Automobile was formed in 1993 with the aim of producing 50,000 cars per year, but a new government policy issued in 1994 on the automobile industry has put those plans on hold.
